NVDA stock was up 2% in Wednesday premarket trading. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) **DSX POD** The company [introduced DSX POD](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4655023-nvidia-targets-faster-ai-infrastructure-rollouts-with-new-dsx-pod-design?utm_source=tradingview&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news), a reference design for AI data centers built in modular containers and assembled and tested before delivery. highlights.content: ![AiThority](https://aithority.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/AIT_1-1.png) [![AiThority](https://aithority.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/AIT_1-1.png) AiThority - Artificial Intelligence | News | Insights | AiThority](https://aithority.com/) ![AiThority](https://aithority.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/AIT_1-1.png) ![AiThority](https://aithority.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/AIT_1-1.png) # HPE Spaceborne Computer to Power High Performance Computing and AI on the Moon ![](https://aithority.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/bwire-150x65.png) #### Hewlett Packard Enterprise Logo ![Hewlett Packard Enterprise Logo]() #### ***NASA, Deloitte, and HPE to deploy AI workloads on HPE’s Spaceborne Computer-4 to maximize the mission’s scientific discovery*** #### ***With 70 years of leadership in space exploration, HPE ushers in a new era by providing the advanced computing foundation for the emerging lunar economy*** #### ***HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 plans to power the first high performance computing benchmarks on the lunar surface*** #### ***HPE Spaceborne Computer-4 will test large language model (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation, vision inference, and LiDAR data for reliable deployment of AI on the Moon*** [HPE](https://www.hpe.com/us/en/home.html) announced HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced compute module built for space environments, plans to power artificial intelligence (AI) and the first high performance computing (HPC) benchmarks on the surface of the Moon1. The system will deploy on Astrolab’s FLIP rover for an upcoming mission for the Moon Base program and will test the suitability of advanced computing for future missions and the emerging lunar economy. **Also Read: [AiThority Interview with Michael Kwok, Vice President, IBM Bob, and Canada Lab Director](https://aithority.com/interviews/aithority-interview-with-michael-kwok-vice-president-ibm-bob-and-canada-lab-director/)** “For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world’s most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery.” “For more than 70 years, HPE innovation has supported some of the world’s most important space missions. The next chapter of lunar exploration will depend on the ability to turn data into insights at the point of discovery,” said Scott Wiest, vice president, fellow and global sales chief technologist, HPE. “With HPE Spaceborne Computer-4, we are bringing AI and high performance computing to the lunar edge, helping the acceleration of scientific discovery and building the infrastructure for the next era of exploration.” The mission is intended to launch in late 2026 as part of NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative. highlights.titleZh: Krafton launches cost-efficient Raon-1 mini LLM to boost AI use in Korea - CHOSUNBIZ
highlights.content: # Krafton launches cost-efficient Raon-1 mini LLM to boost AI use in Korea By  [Kim Su-jeong](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/kim-sujeong/) Published 2026.10.21. 17:08 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) /Courtesy of Krafton Krafton said on the 21st that it released a preview version of its self-developed high-efficiency large language model (LLM), "Raon-1 mini." Raon-1 mini is a 30 billion (30B) parameter LLM that Krafton independently handled end to end, from model design to training. It supports Korean and English and focuses on achieving both high performance and low operating expense. To that end, Krafton combined a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with its self-developed linear attention technology. By activating only 4 billion (4B) of the total 30 billion parameters needed for a task, it reduced computation to speed up responses and lower inference expense. According to the company, Raon-1 mini showed superior performance compared with overseas models in its class, and on some evaluation metrics reached levels close to large domestic models. In particular, it showed strengths in natural Korean conversation, fast response speed, and accurately following user instructions. The ability to follow complex instructions, such as format specification or persona settings, is key to implementing AI agents that autonomously carry out multi-step tasks. Krafton views not only AI model performance but also expense efficiency in real service environments as a core competitive edge. As AI use expands across industries, the company judges it crucial to maintain high performance while lowering operating expense. The preview version has been released on the global AI open-source platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download it for free and use it not only for research but also for commercial services and product development. Krafton plans to release an official version with improved performance and publish a technical report covering the model's training process and final performance. Lee Kang-uk, Krafton chief AI officer (CAIO), said, "The release of Raon-1 mini is the result of independently developing a competitive language model through Krafton's more than five years of accumulated AI research and development capabilities," and added, "As a cost-effective LLM that raises performance and lowers expense burden, we will broaden the use of AI across various industrial fields." ※ This article has been translated by AI. The dual approach shows NVIDIA hedging its bets across both edge and cloud computing as enterprises figure out where their AI workloads will ultimately run. Google's deployment strategy starts domestic before going global. The initial U.S. rollout next month will be followed by European expansion, though specific timing and regions remain under wraps. The company said on the 21st that it had published a preview version of Raon-1 mini, a large language model with 30 billion parameters. Released ahead of the official launch, the model is distributed on Hugging Face, the global AI platform, under an Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download it free of charge and use it not only for research but also for commercial services and product development. Raon-1 mini is a 30-billion-parameter model that Krafton built on its own from design through initial training, and it supports Korean and English. To improve both performance and inference efficiency, Krafton combined a mixture-of-experts architecture with linear attention technology it developed itself. The approach activates only 4 billion of the 30 billion parameters needed for a given task, cutting the volume of computation. That speeds up responses and lowers inference costs, the company said. The preview version of Raon-1 mini outperforms overseas models of comparable size and comes close to larger domestic models on some metrics, according to the company. It is particularly strong at natural conversation in Korean and responds quickly. It also performs well at following instructions precisely, such as specifying formats or adopting a persona. Instruction-following is essential for agent applications, in which a model handles multistep tasks on its own. Krafton pointed to cost efficiency as the core strength of the model. As AI use spreads across industries, the company judged, performance relative to cost in real operating environments matters as much as performance alone. The preview model was therefore developed with a focus on Korean-language conversation, AI agent capability and fast response times. Krafton plans to keep updating Raon-1 mini to improve its performance before releasing an official version. When that version is released, the company will also publish a technical report detailing the model's training process and final performance. "The release of Raon-1 mini is the result of Krafton independently developing a competitive language model with AI research and development capabilities built up over more than five years," said Lee Kang-wook, Krafton's chief AI officer. "With a cost-effective large language model that raises performance while lowering the cost burden, we will widen the scope of AI use across a range of industries." Krafton is also continuing research into the core technologies underpinning AI...

highlights.content: ##### Report GitHub Issue Content selection saved. Describe the issue below: ![archive](https://static.arxiv.org/static/design-system/latest/logos/arxiv-logo.svg) # Beyond Calibration: Temporal LLM Confidence Assessment Across Languages and Local Settings ###### Abstract Large language models are expected to estimate their own uncertainty, with confidence signals used to guide retrieval, adaptive compute allocation, routing, and selective abstention. We investigate whether confidence signals measured at different temporal stages of problem solving encode distinct forms of epistemic information and remain reliable beyond English-centric settings. Inspired by classical meta-memory theory, we distinguish anticipatory pre-solve confidence (*Feeling-of-Knowing*, FOK) from retrospective post-solve confidence (*Judgement-of-Learning*, JOL). We evaluate these signals across two frontier LLMs, multiple reasoning domains, translated Marathi benchmarks, and a newly constructed benchmark of genuinely local Marathi factual questions. Across settings, the cheaper pre-solve signal remains weakly calibrated, while post-solve confidence generally provides stronger epistemic alignment despite its additional inference cost. Confidence behaviour transfers surprisingly well under direct language translation, with calibration trends largely preserved between English and Marathi, but degrades substantially on local Marathi knowledge, suggesting that linguistic transfer alone is insufficient for region-specific information needs. Finally, hallucinated responses maintain persistently elevated confidence after answer generation, highlighting important limitations of current LLM self-assessment mechanisms. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across a wide range of real-world applications, including question answering, reasoning systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), autonomous agents, and decision-support pipelines [Li et al. (2024)](#bib.bib2); [Cheng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1). Modern models contain substantial factual and procedural knowledge encoded within their parameters, while also leveraging external context through tools, retrieval systems, and long-context prompting. In many such systems, models are further expected to make decisions about their own uncertainty and knowledge limitations, a capability often framed as self-knowledge [Kale and Nadadur (2025)](#bib.bib3) or metacognition [Ma et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5). These internal confidence estimates are increasingly used to influence downstream behaviours such as deciding whether to invoke tools, request additional user clarification, defer generation, allocate additional compute, or trigger retrieval mechanisms [Li et al. (2025)](#bib.bib4). However, recent work has shown that LLM confidence signals are often poorly calibrated and only weakly aligned with actual correctness. This limits the efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of such confidence-driven decision policies [Kale and Dhami (2025)](#bib.bib6). ![Refer to caption](2610.27702v1/media/conf_fig1.png) While confidence calibration has been studied primarily in English-centric benchmarks, many practical deployments increasingly involve multilingual and underrepresented language settings where both model knowledge and evaluation resources are less abundant. Confidence estimates that appear reliable in high-resource settings may fail to transfer across languages or culturally specific knowledge domains, potentially leading to inappropriate retrieval decisions, overconfident hallucinations, or unsafe downstream behaviour. A particularly important open question is whether confidence calibration is primarily tied to language or to underlying knowledge availability. A model may retain similar confidence behaviour when questions are translated into another language, yet fail when confronted with genuinely local information that is sparsely represented in pre-training corpora and evaluation ...

AI Agents.content: [Infosecurity Magazine Home](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/) » [Opinions](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/opinions/) » [What Amazon's Blocking of Meta’s AI Shopping Agent Reveals About Current Identity Protocols](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/opinions/amazon-metas-ai-shopping-agent/) # What Amazon's Blocking of Meta’s AI Shopping Agent Reveals About Current Identity Protocols [Opinion](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/opinions/) ## Written by ![Photo of Sharat Menon](https://assets.infosecurity-magazine.com/s3/infosec-media/images/profile/33a89a06-00ba-4bd9-bd39-9535483d35dd.jpeg?width=64&height=64&mode=crop&scale=both&format=webp) ### [Sharat Menon](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/profile/sharat-menon/) Engineering Manager, AI Security Platform, Schneider Electric Amazon recently blocked Muse, Meta’s AI shopping agent, from making purchases on its site. According to Amazon, Meta never requested access to its store, Muse doesn’t identify itself as an agent while browsing, and it appears to capture and store customer credentials, all without Amazon’s knowledge or consent. Meta counters that credentials go into secure storage the model itself never reads. Amazon’s terms now require agents to identify themselves via a text snippet in HTTP requests; Muse doesn’t send one. Strip away the corporate sparring and this is a familiar security problem wearing a new outfit: one organization’s autonomous software is acting inside another organization’s systems, and there’s no shared way to establish who, or what, is actually there. We solved this for humans years ago. OIDC and SAML let you log into a partner’s application without that partner managing your password, because there’s an agreed protocol for asserting identity and federating trust across organizational boundaries. That protocol doesn’t yet exist, in any adopted form, for agents. And the industry knows it. The OpenID Foundation published a whitepaper, Identity Management for Agentic AI, alongside concrete draft extensions like OIDC-A, which propose agent-specific claims and delegation chains on top of standard OpenID Connect. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)’s National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence put out a [concept paper](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/other/2026/02/05/accelerating-the-adoption-of-software-and-ai-agent/ipd) on agent identity and authorization. AI Agents.titleZh: Walmart announces AI agent and gateway shopping tools
AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#primary) [![Ice, Nature, Outdoors, Text, Sea, Water](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20362%2090'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://dig.watch/) [Digital Watch Observatory](https://dig.watch/) Digital Governance in 50+ issues, 500+ actors, 5+ processes [Subscribe](#contact-hub) # Walmart announces AI Agent and Gateway shopping tools *Walmart announced the launch of ‘Agent Profiles’ and a ‘Walmart Agent Gateway’, enabling authorised AI agents to shop and complete purchases for customers.* ![ Electronics, Mobile Phone, Phone, Iphone](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%200%200'%3E%3C/svg%3E) image via unsplash On 21 October 2026, Walmart [announced](https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2026/10/Making-It-Possible-for-Agents-to-Shop-on-Behalf-of-Customers) that it will introduce new tools that enable AI agents to shop and complete transactions for customers. The tools are being made available to all Walmart account holders and will not require a Walmart+ membership. The retailer also announced that customers will be able to monitor purchases made by [AI agents](https://dig.watch/topics/consumer-protection) apart from their own orders and can revoke an agent’s access at any time. Walmart added that the ‘Agent Profiles’ feature will be rolled out in the next month. Agent Profiles will allow shoppers to authorise individual AI agents, track the agents’ purchases separately, and set a spending limit or require approval for each transaction. The company also launched the ‘Walmart Agent Gateway’, a platform that lets AI assistants such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini and Meta’s Muse connect directly with Walmart and Sam’s Club systems to search for products and complete purchases. In September Meta launched its AI personal agent, Muse, that performs multi‑step tasks and connects to different services including shopping. Shortly after Amazon [announced](https://dig.watch/updates/amazon-blocks-metas-muse-ai-from-shopping-site) that it had blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com. Amazon has been actively limiting unauthorised AI agents on its platform, however its own AI‑driven shopping tools include Alexa for Shopping, and the Buy for Me feature, which identifies itself and allows brands to opt out. It has been [reported](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/banks-warn-ai-shopping-bots-raise-scam-fraud-data-privacy-risks-2026-09-22/) that banks issued warnings about the risks of using AI agents for online shopping; these risks include scams, fraud and ​data-privacy breaches. In terms of security features, Walmart said that customers will remain in control of purchases, that AI agents will be barred from accessing payment‑card data, and that agents that breach the stated terms will be blocked from the site. ## Why does it matter? The announcement by Walmart demonstrates the continued adoption of the latest AI-shopping digital business model. Agentic AI shopping is an online retail model where autonomous AI agents search, compare, and complete purchases for users with minimal manual effort. Major platforms like ChatGPT, Google, and Meta already feature built-in agentic checkout and personal shopping assistants. It is noted that financial institutions have voiced concerns that the rapid deployment of autonomous systems, in particular agentic commerce, currently outpace the implementation of appropriate safety guardrails. On that front, some progress is being made with the introduction of [proposed legislation](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5051?s=1&r=35) to address the risks posed by autonomous agents, but for the most part there continues to be reliance on current consumer protection laws and [data protection](https://dig.watch/updates/ico-data-protection-changes-from-ai-developers) frameworks to fill in some of the gaps. AI Agents.content: [The Independent Voice on AI](https://venturebeat.com/) * [Orchestration](https://venturebeat.com/category/orchestration) * [Infrastructure](https://venturebeat.com/category/infrastructure) * [Data](https://venturebeat.com/category/data) * [Security](https://venturebeat.com/category/security) * [Technology](https://venturebeat.com/category/technology) More [Newsletters](https://venturebeat.com/newsletters) # Researchers made AI agents better by turning academic papers into working code — no retraining required [Ben Dickson](https://venturebeat.com/author/ben-dickson-techtalks) 2:42 pm, PT, October 21, 2026 ![Image 1: AI harness optimization](https://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2FCQGZ4flW7w5g88Y4qcC8l%2Fa35201e5031cd5770c37d861106c934a%2FAI_harness_optimization.jpeg%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=85) Image credit: VentureBeat with Gemini AI agents are being given the ability to optimize their own components, such as prompts, context management, workflows, and code. However, current self-evolving harness optimizers usually draw on the pre-existing knowledge of the underlying models or trajectories that the agent has explored so far. A new framework developed by researchers at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Microsoft addresses this bottleneck. Dubbed [ScholarEvolve](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40169), the framework automatically extracts new information from research papers and translates it into code upgrades for an agent’s harness. In benchmark tests, ScholarEvolve boosted the open-weight Qwen3.5-27B model from 69.0% to 81.4% task completion on the AppWorld Normal test set, closing roughly 74% of the performance gap with GPT-5.4 without updating the model’s weights. For enterprise engineering teams, the approach offers a path to improve agent performance without retraining the underlying models, while also establishing a blueprint for continuous harness upgrades that adapt to unfamiliar APIs. ## Where current harness optimizers hit a wall Over the past year, automated harness optimization frameworks have generally followed one of two paths. Component-specific tools, such as [Google’s WikiSkill](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/googles-wikiskill-gives-ai-agents-a-memory-of-what-went-wrong-without-putting-it-in-the-prompt), [Microsoft’s SkillOpt](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/microsofts-open-source-skillopt-automatically-upgrades-ai-agent-skills-without-touching-model-weights), and [Memento-Skills](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/new-framework-lets-ai-agents-rewrite-their-own-skills-without-retraining-the), examine the agent’s trajectories to refine a single part of the stack, such as a skill library or memory store. Meanwhile, full-harness optimizers like [Salesforce’s DarwinX](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/salesforce-researchers-took-an-ai-agent-from-finishing-43-5-of-browser-tasks-to-93-without-touching-the-model), [Xiaomi’s HarnessX](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/xiaomis-harnessx-rewrites-its-own-ai-scaffolding-mid-task-and-smaller-models-gain-the-most), [Self-Harness](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/researchers-introduce-self-harness-a-framework-that-lets-ai-agents-rewrite-their-own-rules-boosting-performance-up-to-60), and Stanford’s Meta-Harness use a coding meta-agent to inspect failure traces and rewrite the agent’s scaffolding or operating rules. While these methods are effective, the UCSB and Microsoft researchers argue that relying solely on execution feedback creates a closed loop that quickly reaches a point of diminishing returns. ![Image 2: Meta harness evolution vs external research](https://venturebeat.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2F15u8EoeH39Hoexqa4tr8pO%2Fd65d4d5bb0d0fbd1532c8700e069957b%2Fimage4.png%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=75) Meta harness evolution vs external research (source: arXiv) First, the meta-agent is restricted by the parametric knowledge of th...

LLMs.content: # Krafton launches cost-efficient Raon-1 mini LLM to boost AI use in Korea By  [Kim Su-jeong](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/kim-sujeong/) Published 2026.10.21. 17:08 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) /Courtesy of Krafton Krafton said on the 21st that it released a preview version of its self-developed high-efficiency large language model (LLM), "Raon-1 mini." Raon-1 mini is a 30 billion (30B) parameter LLM that Krafton independently handled end to end, from model design to training. It supports Korean and English and focuses on achieving both high performance and low operating expense. To that end, Krafton combined a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture with its self-developed linear attention technology. By activating only 4 billion (4B) of the total 30 billion parameters needed for a task, it reduced computation to speed up responses and lower inference expense. According to the company, Raon-1 mini showed superior performance compared with overseas models in its class, and on some evaluation metrics reached levels close to large domestic models. In particular, it showed strengths in natural Korean conversation, fast response speed, and accurately following user instructions. The ability to follow complex instructions, such as format specification or persona settings, is key to implementing AI agents that autonomously carry out multi-step tasks. Krafton views not only AI model performance but also expense efficiency in real service environments as a core competitive edge. As AI use expands across industries, the company judges it crucial to maintain high performance while lowering operating expense. The preview version has been released on the global AI open-source platform Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Anyone can download it for free and use it not only for research but also for commercial services and product development. Krafton plans to release an official version with improved performance and publish a technical report covering the model's training process and final performance. Lee Kang-uk, Krafton chief AI officer (CAIO), said, "The release of Raon-1 mini is the result of independently developing a competitive language model through Krafton's more than five years of accumulated AI research and development capabilities," and added, "As a cost-effective LLM that raises performance and lowers expense burden, we will broaden the use of AI across various industrial fields." ※ This article has been translated by AI. LLMs.content: ##### Report GitHub Issue Content selection saved. Describe the issue below: ![archive](https://static.arxiv.org/static/design-system/latest/logos/arxiv-logo.svg) # Beyond Calibration: Temporal LLM Confidence Assessment Across Languages and Local Settings ###### Abstract Large language models are expected to estimate their own uncertainty, with confidence signals used to guide retrieval, adaptive compute allocation, routing, and selective abstention. We investigate whether confidence signals measured at different temporal stages of problem solving encode distinct forms of epistemic information and remain reliable beyond English-centric settings. Inspired by classical meta-memory theory, we distinguish anticipatory pre-solve confidence (*Feeling-of-Knowing*, FOK) from retrospective post-solve confidence (*Judgement-of-Learning*, JOL). We evaluate these signals across two frontier LLMs, multiple reasoning domains, translated Marathi benchmarks, and a newly constructed benchmark of genuinely local Marathi factual questions. Across settings, the cheaper pre-solve signal remains weakly calibrated, while post-solve confidence generally provides stronger epistemic alignment despite its additional inference cost. Confidence behaviour transfers surprisingly well under direct language translation, with calibration trends largely preserved between English and Marathi, but degrades substantially on local Marathi knowledge, suggesting that linguistic transfer alone is insufficient for region-specific information needs. Finally, hallucinated responses maintain persistently elevated confidence after answer generation, highlighting important limitations of current LLM self-assessment mechanisms. ## 1 Introduction Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across a wide range of real-world applications, including question answering, reasoning systems, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), autonomous agents, and decision-support pipelines [Li et al. (2024)](#bib.bib2); [Cheng et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1). Modern models contain substantial factual and procedural knowledge encoded within their parameters, while also leveraging external context through tools, retrieval systems, and long-context prompting. In many such systems, models are further expected to make decisions about their own uncertainty and knowledge limitations, a capability often framed as self-knowledge [Kale and Nadadur (2025)](#bib.bib3) or metacognition [Ma et al. (2025)](#bib.bib5). These internal confidence estimates are increasingly used to influence downstream behaviours such as deciding whether to invoke tools, request additional user clarification, defer generation, allocate additional compute, or trigger retrieval mechanisms [Li et al. (2025)](#bib.bib4). However, recent work has shown that LLM confidence signals are often poorly calibrated and only weakly aligned with actual correctness. This limits the efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of such confidence-driven decision policies [Kale and Dhami (2025)](#bib.bib6). ![Refer to caption](2610.27702v1/media/conf_fig1.png) While confidence calibration has been studied primarily in English-centric benchmarks, many practical deployments increasingly involve multilingual and underrepresented language settings where both model knowledge and evaluation resources are less abundant. Confidence estimates that appear reliable in high-resource settings may fail to transfer across languages or culturally specific knowledge domains, potentially leading to inappropriate retrieval decisions, overconfident hallucinations, or unsafe downstream behaviour. A particularly important open question is whether confidence calibration is primarily tied to language or to underlying knowledge availability. Mistral says its Small model beats Whisper large-v3 on word error rate in FLEURS benchmark tests across 45 languages. ##### Key Elements ![Mistral Launches Voxtral 3 Voice Agent SDK, Enabling Real-Time Interaction in More Than 50 Languages](https://img.biggo.com/atnCPWCDTLQ7E9KfoG91LzG3wvhN2MqceTAj23hqDg8/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwL2Y3NDZmYTA3LTY5NDctNGMzNC1iMWQ3LWRhNTFkOTM0MGE1N18xNzkyNTY5ODA1X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI on October 20 released a voice agent software development kit (SDK) and a companion family of speech models, Voxtral 3, integrating speech recognition, reasoning and decision-making, tool calling and speech synthesis into a single real-time processing pipeline aimed at call centers, help desks, virtual assistants and similar use cases. The product supports transcription in more than 50 languages and speech synthesis in more than 35 languages. It is available immediately through European, U.S. and global APIs and also supports enterprise self-hosted deployment. Unlike offerings on the market that stitch together separate transcription, synthesis and reasoning components, Voxtral 3 emphasizes an "end-to-end connected" capability. According to a report by OSChina, in an official demonstration an English-speaking user called a clinic holding a French-language referral letter; the voice agent recognized the French content, completed the appointment and promised to send a confirmation text message in English, showcasing a complete workflow combining cross-language understanding, tool calling and emotional adaptation. At the model level, the transcription products come in three versions. Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 and Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 cover more than 50 languages; the former offers speaker diarization, preset specialized terminology to improve recognition accuracy, and end-of-speech detection. Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3, aimed at real-time scenarios, has latency below 500 milliseconds. The speech synthesis model Voxtral Speech 3 supports more than 35 languages and more than 50 dialects, and can adjust emotion, speaking rate and accent based on conversational context. Mistral AI says that in FLEURS benchmark tests across 45 languages, Small's word error rate outperforms competitors such as Whisper large-v3. The SDK runs on LiveKit, allowing end-of-speech detection, inference by a general-purpose model (such as Mistral Small) and tool calling, and voice responses to proceed in parallel without waiting for the previous step to finish. A single interaction turn completes within one second, and the system stops speaking when the user interrupts. At the interface level, it supports telephone lines (SIP) and WebRTC and can connect to existing call-center software. The typical case is mundane: a marketer pastes a client brief into a personal ChatGPT account. The term exists because generative AI put a powerful data-processing service in reach of anyone with a browser, and data typed into it leaves the company's control the moment it is sent. IBM defines it as "the unsanctioned use of any artificial intelligence (AI) tool or application" by employees or end users without formal approval from the IT department. It is a branch of **shadow IT**, with one difference: an unapproved AI tool does not only store data but processes it, may retain it and may train on it. ## How shadow AI enters an organisation Shadow AI arrives through several channels. * **Personal accounts on public chatbots.** An employee uses ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek through a private email address. The account sits outside the company's contract, retention settings and audit logs. * **Copy and paste.** Much data reaches AI tools through the clipboard, which older data loss prevention (DLP) tools, built to watch attachments and uploads, often miss. * **Browser extensions.** Assistants that read the page being viewed, often with broad permissions. * **AI features switched on inside approved software.** An approved vendor adds a generative feature in an update, creating a data flow no one reviewed. * **Agents and connectors.** Since 2025, employees can connect assistants to calendars, drives and ad accounts through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for linking AI models to external tools. AI Product.content: # AI Research Startup Flapping Airplanes Valued at $6 Billion Flapping Airplanes, a year-old artificial intelligence startup, has raised $1 billion in funding at a $6 billion valuation — the latest example of investors betting on a newer crop of AI research labs that have yet to introduce commercial products. The financing, set to be announced Wednesday, was led by Index Ventures and Lux Capital. Other participants included Sequoia Capital, Alphabet Inc.’s GV and Kleiner Perkins. The company’s valuation, which includes the money raised, has quadrupled from a prior round in January. Founded in late 2025, Flapping Airplanes is one of a growing number of so-called AI neolabs, or startups that are initially focused on research rather than racing to launch artificial intelligence products and bolster revenue. Venture capital firms have poured billions of dollars into companies working on AI-driven scientific breakthroughs, self-improving AI systems and more. Flapping Airplanes is working on methods to train AI models on less data and less compute, as well as making the chips used to develop and run models more efficient, co-founder Asher Spector said in an interview. The effort to do more with less coincides with heightened scrutiny on the massive amount of capital companies are spending on chips and data centers to support AI development. “The basic thesis is demand for AI is going to outpace chip and data supply,” Spector said. “The company that’s going to be most successful, and create the most value for the world, is the one that can squeeze the most out of the inputs.” Given how much money is being spent on infrastructure for the current AI boom, wringing 10% more performance out of each chip would be “tremendously economically valuable,” he said.

Open Source AI.titleZh: Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval
Open Source AI.content: [Skip to Main Navigation](#main) [![World Bank Blogs Logo](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/logo-en?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2 "World Bank Blogs Logo")](/en/home) Published on [Data Blog](/en/opendata) # Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval * [Rafael Sevilla Macalaba](/en/team/r/rafael-sevilla-macalaba) * [Aivin Solatorio](/en/team/a/aivin-solatorio) This page in: * [English](/en/opendata/beyond-chat-demos--evaluating-llm-systems-at-scale-with-deepeval) * [English](/en/opendata/beyond-chat-demos--evaluating-llm-systems-at-scale-with-deepeval) ![Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/generative-ai-1?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2 "Beyond chat demos: evaluating LLM systems at scale with DeepEval") The evaluation framework combines persona composition, live multi-turn simulation, metric pre-filtering, and LLM-based scoring to test chatbot reliability at scale. / Image: Shutterstock Building a generative AI chat prototype has become straightforward. With a large language model (LLM), a vector database, a frontend interface, and an AI coding assistant, a developer can assemble a working demo in days. However, deploying such applications at institutions like the World Bank Group—where data accuracy, policy context, and citation verifiability are essential—requires far more than a working proof of concept. How do you guarantee an LLM assistant remains reliable across hundreds of user requests? How do you ensure it does not hallucinate indicators, skip citations, or lose context over multi-turn dialogues? How do you measure response quality for questions users have not yet asked? To address these challenges, we built an automated, persona-driven evaluation framework using Confident AI's open-source [DeepEval](https://deepeval.com/) library as our scoring backbone. While DeepEval provides core metric primitives, our framework introduces custom innovations: dynamic persona composition, intelligent pre-filtering, and a replay mechanism for rapid rubric iteration. Originally created for the Data360 Chat Assistant, this framework is now packaged as a reusable blueprint for building trustworthy AI applications across the institution ([GitHub Repository](https://github.com/worldbank/data-ai-chatbot)). ### The unpredictable path of multi-turn chat Traditional software testing is linear: input A yields output B. For conversational AI, this approach fails because user interactions are dynamic, branching dialogues. A user might greet the assistant, ask for GDP trends, request data formatted in a table, compare neighboring countries, and finally request a chart. ![Image](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/Screenshot-2026-10-21-152106?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2) Conversation Turn Progression Evaluating isolated responses misses compounding multi-turn failures: * **Context Drift:** The model forgets constraints (such as country or year range) specified in earlier turns. * **Orchestration Failures:** The router correctly classifies intent on Turn 1 but strays onto an incorrect path on Turn 3. * **State and Transport Breaks:** Persistent Server-Sent Events (SSE) data streams can cut off mid-transit, or database session state can fail to reload, forcing the model to restart. To catch these failures, our framework executes tests directly against the live chatbot API—requesting guest auth tokens, persisting PostgreSQL session IDs, and parsing streamed responses to simulate real user sessions. ![Image](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/Screenshot-2026-10-21-152125?qlt=90&fmt=webp&resMode=sharp2) Chatbot Evaluation System Dataflow ### From isolation to standardization Across large organizations, teams build specialized GenAI applications to query databases, summarize documents, or scan research. On Tuesday, the Chinese AI lab [published DeepInfer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer), the inference framework behind its large-scale production services, as open-source code under the Apache 2.0 license, with Huawei’s Ascend 950 chips supported alongside Nvidia’s newest GPUs. ![DeepSeek V4 - artistic interpretation. Image credit: Alius Noreika / AI](https://www.technology.org/texorgwp/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/deepseek-ai-software-model-v4-photo.jpg) ![DeepSeek V4 - artistic interpretation. Image credit: Alius Noreika / AI](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%201365%201006%22%3E%3C/svg%3E) ### **Key Takeaways** ## What Comes in the Box DeepInfer bundles optimized kernels from DeepSeek’s earlier open projects, including FlashMLA, DeepGEMM and DeepEP, plus TileKernels, DeepSelect and custom TileLang kernels. It spreads work across chips with attention data parallelism, balanced context parallelism, and expert parallelism for mixture-of-experts layers with load balancing (EPLB). A decoding method called DSpark drafts tokens ahead and uses confidence estimates to decide when to verify them. By default it drafts up to five tokens. Other features include bounded replay for sliding-window attention, which trims prefill work, and an asynchronous scheduler that overlaps CPU batch planning with chip execution. Developers can also force outputs into a regex, JSON schema or EBNF grammar. Two features, batch-invariant inference and deterministic sampling, work on Nvidia hardware only. They keep results identical across runs with the same inputs. DeepSeek also published deepseek-recipe, a component that turns text into tokens and back the same way its official API does. Open Source AI.content: security # LiteLLM supply chain attack hoovers up passwords and secrets Plus a RAT for good measure - get threat hunting now ### READ MORE * #### Auto tech startup claims it traced hack attempt back to rival's IP address * #### Palo Alto's firewall OS has been under attack from multiple ransomware groups since June * #### 'Password1' and a forgotten test account land Welsh outfits in hot water * #### Broadcom Wi-Fi bug turns sweet 16, still lets strangers hijack your router * #### ConnectWise turns off its SaaS-y backup, security, and management services to probe security SNAFU Unknown crims compromised LiteLLM's release process on Wednesday, distributing a malicious version (1.107.0) containing malware designed to steal cloud and AI credentials and a remote access trojan (RAT) capable of executing arbitrary code on infected machines through PyPI and Docker registries. PyPI quarantined the trojanized version of the popular open source AI gateway within hours, and the Docker image (litellm/litellm:1.107.0) was removed from both Docker Hub and GHCR soon after - but anyone who ran the compromised package on any platform should assume their secrets have been stolen. “Check for /tmp/.pc\_once\_\* (the exfil has already fired if this file exists) and /tmp/remote\_code\_loader.lock (the C2 daemon ran or is still running if this file exists),” advised Aikido Security malware hunter Ilyas Makari. “The same applies to anyone who ran the official Docker image litellm/litellm:1.107.0, or pulled it via the latest, main-latest, or main-stable tags.” The most recent safe version is v1.106.2. While it’s too early to tell the scale of this latest LiteLLM supply chain attack – an earlier LiteLLM compromise in March potentially exposed more than 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines worldwide, according to CloudSEK – make sure to take these measures seriously, and check environments for any indicators of compromise. Aikido, Google’s Wiz cloud security biz, and supply-chain security provider Socket have all published extensive threat-hunting and mitigation instructions for LiteLLM users and security teams, so give those a read stat. LiteLLM, developed by BerriAI, provides a common interface for LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini, and receives about 23 million weekly downloads. This means a compromised installation can run alongside LLM provider API keys, cloud identities, and database connection strings - and expose a ton of valuable credentials, secrets, and other sensitive data to whoever uploaded the malicious package. “Teams using 1.107.0 should stop deploying it and investigate environments where Python ran after installation, including proxy containers and CI runners,” Socket researchers said on Wednesday. The malicious version was uploaded at 11:39 UTC, and according to Wiz kids Benjamin Read and Rami McCarthy, the payload originates with malicious commits made on github.com/Berri-AI/litellm, which is a hyphenated variant of the legitimate BerriAI organization. Miscreants used this repo to inject the three malicious files into the LiteLLM release pipeline. These, according to Makari, include cook.pth, which causes the second file, cook.py, to run automatically every time Python is invoked on the machine, without any additional user action. Meanwhile, cook.py contains the infostealer, and the third file, sitecustomize.py, is the RAT. Python also executes the RAT at interpreter startup, and this file spawns a background daemon that polls the attacker's infrastructure every hour for new commands to execute. Upon executing, the infostealer harvests a ton of sensitive data across 16 modules targeting browsers, cloud providers, and AI services, according to Read and McCarthy. It steals browser credentials and cookies from Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari, along with AWS credentials from ~/.aws/, environment variables, and EC2/ECS instance metadata (IMDS). Isolate, Rebuild and Rotate Now](https://www.rescana.com/post/img/litellm-1-107-0-supply-chain-compromise-october-2026-cover-v1.png) **TL;DR:** On 21 October 2026, LiteLLM's release pipeline was compromised and published **LiteLLM v1.107.0** to PyPI and Docker with "compiled malware which steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools" ([LiteLLM incident report](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-incident-oct-21-2026)). The PyPI wheels were live from **11:39 to 13:23 UTC (14:39 to 16:23 Cyprus time (UTC+3))**, and the Docker tags **v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable** pointed to the malicious image from **11:46 to 14:20 UTC (14:46 to 17:20 Cyprus time (UTC+3))**. LiteLLM says all previous versions are safe, the impacted releases have been pulled, and customers on its private enterprise release were not impacted. If any system installed 1.107.0 or started one of those images in the window, LiteLLM says to **assume it is compromised**. There is no CVE for this incident. Wiz says it has "observed abuse of stolen credentials", starting about 4.5 hours after exfiltration ([Wiz](https://www.wiz.io/blog/litellm-compromised-steals-credentials)). **Isolate affected hosts, rebuild them from clean images, and rotate every credential they could reach.** LiteLLM is an open-source Python SDK and proxy (AI gateway) that sits in front of LLM providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini. Because it usually runs next to provider API keys, cloud identities and database connection strings, a compromised install can expose exactly the secrets an attacker wants. Socket says LiteLLM "receives approximately 23M weekly downloads" ([Socket](https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise)). ## **Exposure Windows** All times are from LiteLLM's incident report (21 October 2026). | Artifact | Affected | Window (UTC) | Window (Cyprus time, UTC+3) | Status (per LiteLLM) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | PyPI | litellm==1.107.0, all seven wheels | 11:39:51 to 13:23 | 14:39:51 to 16:23 | Pulled from PyPI | | Docker Hub (docker.io/litellm/litellm) | Tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, main-stable | 11:46:56 to 14:20 | 14:46:56 to 17:20 | v1.107.0 removed; other tags re-pointed to verified clean artifacts | | GHCR (ghcr.io/berriai/litellm, litellm-database, litellm-non\_root) | Tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, main-stable | 11:46:56 to 13:51 | 14:46:56 to 16:51 | Made unavailable by 13:51 UTC | LiteLLM's compromised Docker Hub image index digest is **sha256:1bbcb1443bc962e45f5aad53fe3d2c30600e0379715fb6c664cdd3ac126c339e**. On all four images, latest, main-latest and main-stable now resolve to the same image index as that image's v1.106.2 tag (docker.io/litellm/litellm and ghcr.io/berriai/litellm sha256:7294b90f868c5c38c99b83021c7ba46f9b439e95f8e32964c925c7d2563a03f7; litellm-database sha256:35f2cec3a14bb297e08bfab56c1fc377432bc4071aaf71978fdff043a5d91e79; litellm-non\_root sha256:07fabea33dfc2b127e865c03112dfc76936334b29028ec05cdd355af2385dc04). NVDA stock was up 2% in Wednesday premarket trading. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) **DSX POD** The company [introduced DSX POD](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4655023-nvidia-targets-faster-ai-infrastructure-rollouts-with-new-dsx-pod-design?utm_source=tradingview&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news), a reference design for AI data centers built in modular containers and assembled and tested before delivery. Nvidia said the approach could cut deployment time at prepared sites from six months to as little as 14 days. Partners include Dell [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/dell.svg)DELL](/symbols/NYSE-DELL/), Hewlett Packard Enterprise [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/hewlett-packard-enterprise.svg)HPE](/symbols/NYSE-HPE/), Lenovo, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/vertiv-holdings.svg)VRT](/symbols/NYSE-VRT/). ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/dell.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/hewlett-packard-enterprise.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/vertiv-holdings.svg) Nvidia said European partners are adopting its DSX AI Factory Platform to build data centers that use less cooling water and less power for the same AI output. **SUPPLY CHAIN** Nvidia said it is working with supply chain partners to expand capacity: Nvidia is expanding manufacturing capacity [with $1.3B deal](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4655102-amkor-shares-jump-10-percent-on-1_3b-nvidia-agreement?utm_source=tradingview&utm_medium=referral&feed_item_type=news) with Amkor [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amkor-technology.svg)AMKR](/symbols/NASDAQ-AMKR/) to increase advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amkor-technology.svg) Infineon [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/infineon-technologies.svg)IFNNY](/symbols/OTC-IFNNY/) is advancing its collaboration with Nvidia on gallium nitride-based intermediate bus converter solutions for 800 VDC AI data center power architectures. Infra & Chips.content: ![country_code](https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/1x1-00000000.png) [Skip to content](#primary) # NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by [Stuart Pitts](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/author/stuartpitts/ "Posts by Stuart Pitts") [0 Comments](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents/#disqus_thread) Share This Article * [X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F) * [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F) * [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fblogs.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fcloud-partners-europe-sovereign-safety-open-agents%2F&title=NVIDIA+Cloud+Partners+Scale+Across+Europe+%E2%80%94+Sovereign%2C+Open+and+Built+for+Safe+AI+Agents+%7C+NVIDIA+Blog) * [Copy link Link copied!](# "Copy link to clipboard") ![](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ai-cloud-announcement-gtc-berlin-social-1920x1080-5852877-r2-1280x720.png) Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design.  [NVIDIA Cloud Partners](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/gpu-cloud-computing/partners/) across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. [Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements](https://blogs.nvidia.com/gtc-berlin-2026-news/) ## **Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure** Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the [NVIDIA DSX Platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/dsx/maxlps/) to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget.  Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Edited by Barnabas Oretan (The Tech Buzz).· AI-generated image [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com) and [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com) are bringing the chipmaker's Vera Rubin infrastructure to general availability next month, marking a significant escalation in the cloud AI arms race. The A5X instances combine NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and Google's fourth-generation liquid-cooling technology, creating an integrated platform for AI training, inference, and large-scale reinforcement learning. The rollout starts in the U.S. before expanding to Europe, as hyperscalers race to offer the most powerful AI infrastructure to enterprise customers. [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com) is making its biggest bet yet on AI infrastructure, announcing that [NVIDIA's](https://www.nvidia.com) Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances will reach general availability next month. The move puts Google squarely in competition with rivals racing to offer the most powerful cloud-based AI training platforms. The A5X instances represent a full-stack approach to AI infrastructure. They bring together NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 GPUs, the company's ConnectX-9 SuperNICs for high-speed networking, Google Cloud's proprietary Virgo Network, and Google's fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology. It's an integrated system designed for the most demanding AI workloads, from training massive models to running inference at scale and handling complex reinforcement learning tasks. The timing couldn't be more strategic. Just hours after [NVIDIA unveiled its full local AI stack at GTC Berlin](https://www.techbuzz.ai/articles/nvidia-unleashes-full-local-ai-stack-at-gtc-berlin), including RTX Spark and DGX systems for on-device intelligence, the company is now extending its reach into cloud infrastructure. The dual approach shows NVIDIA hedging its bets across both edge and cloud computing as enterprises figure out where their AI workloads will ultimately run. Google's deployment strategy starts domestic before going global. The initial U.S. rollout next month will be followed by European expansion, though specific timing and regions remain under wraps. The phased approach suggests Google is being cautious about scaling what's essentially a complex, power-hungry infrastructure play that requires significant data center modifications. Advertisement The liquid-cooling component is particularly telling. Google's fourth-generation cooling technology isn't just about keeping chips from overheating - it's about density. Modern AI accelerators generate so much heat that traditional air cooling can't pack them close enough together for optimal performance. When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select * [Downloads](https://software.cisco.com/download/navigator.html) * [Certifications](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/learn/training-certifications/index.html) * [Design Guides](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/solutions/design-zone.html) * [Training](https://learninglocator.cloudapps.cisco.com/#/home) * [Community](https://community.cisco.com/) * [Careers](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/about/careers.html) ![](https://blogs.cisco.com/wp-content/themes/ciscowordpress-child/svg/search_background.svg) # Cisco Blogs [Cisco Blogs](https://blogs.cisco.com) [Executive Platform](https://blogs.cisco.com/news) # Turn Distributed Capacity into AI Infrastructure [![Author](https://blogs.cisco.com/gcs/ciscoblogs/1/2022/06/IL20220606160354-Gurudatt-Shenoy-150x150.jpg)](https://blogs.cisco.com/author/gshenoy) [Gurudatt Shenoy](https://blogs.cisco.com/author/gshenoy) [Executive Platform](https://blogs.cisco.com/news) October 21, 2026 • 5 min read • 8 min listen ![](https://blogs.cisco.com/gcs/ciscoblogs/1/2026/10/IL20261016234411-AdobeStock_277397261-scaled-600x200.jpeg) For service providers, AI creates a familiar strategic question. Will the network carry someone else’s value, or will it become the platform on which that value is created? Inference gives service providers a strong opportunity to choose the second path. They already have assets that the AI economy needs: distributed facilities, power, trusted infrastructure, and reach in the regions where enterprises and governments operate. Those assets become more valuable when they can operate as one system. An inference request may have suitable capacity near by, yet still travel farther than necessary because the network does not have enough context about the workload. The best destination may depend on latency, available throughput, cost, or a jurisdictional requirement. Conventional reachability alone does not express all those needs. At [NVIDIA GTC](https://www.nvidia.com/gtc/) Berlin, Cisco is [introducing a blueprint for AI Inference Routing,](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/solutions/collateral/design-zone/ai-inference-wan-wp.html) one of several areas where Cisco and NVIDIA are working together for service providers. It outlines how service providers can place, route, secure, and assure inference across a distributed footprint, from a single edge site to a sovereign regional hub. The goal is to solve utilization through placement and routing rather than more infrastructure. Capacity sitting idle in one region can be applied to demand in another, and the resulting service can be built on demand rather than pre-provisioned site by site. ## **Why inference changes the role of the network** An AI prompt may look like a simple exchange between a user and a model, but the underlying transaction crosses a distributed system. It can [pass through the Internet or an enterprise network, policy engines, API gateways, model-routing layers, CPU serving infrastructure, and a GPU fabric before the response returns](https://blogs.cisco.com/sp/why-ai-inference-is-becoming-a-networking-issue). That makes placement and connectivity part of the application experience. This matters even more as inference spreads across central AI factories, regional data centers, metro locations, and edge sites. One request may need the lowest-delay path. Another may need to remain within a national boundary. A third may prioritize cost while still meeting a performance objective. Service providers need a way to translate those requirements into network behavior, and to verify with measurement that the service is delivering what was committed...
